questions.stem: A 10-turn coil has flux change 0.05 Wb in 0.25 s; find induced emf.
questions.explanation: emf = N dPhi/dt = 10*0.05/0.25 = 2.0 V. Forgetting N gives 0.2 V.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Predict current direction for withdrawn magnet
questions.stem: A north pole is withdrawn from a coil; the induced near face becomes...

options.text: No pole, since flux is zero
North, to repel the receding pole
South, to attract the receding pole
Either, depending on speed

questions.explanation: Withdrawing reduces flux; induced field attracts the receding pole, so near face is south. Repulsion would worsen the loss.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute emf for tilted velocity
questions.stem: A 1.0 m rod moves at 5 m/s; velocity makes 30 deg with 0.4 T field; find emf.
questions.explanation: Only perpendicular component matters: v_perp = 5 sin30 = 2.5 m/s; emf = 0.4*1.0*2.5 = 1.0 V. Using full v gives 2.0 V.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute mutual inductance concept
questions.stem: Mutual inductance between two coils is large when...

options.text: Their turn counts are both zero
They are far apart with no shared flux
Their resistances are both high
They are close and well coupled magnetically

questions.explanation: Mutual inductance depends on shared flux, which is large for close, well-coupled coils. Distance and resistance do not help.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute peak current from peak emf
questions.stem: Peak emf 120 V drives a 30 ohm load; find peak current.
questions.explanation: I_peak = V_peak/R = 120/30 = 4.0 A. Using rms voltage would give 2.83 A.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute emf for sinusoidal flux
questions.stem: Flux Phi=0.1 sin(100 t) Wb; find peak induced emf.
questions.explanation: emf = -dPhi/dt = -0.1*100 cos(100t); peak = 10 V. Using 0.1 sin amplitude directly is wrong.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute turns needed for target inductance
questions.stem: To double inductance of a solenoid without changing length or area, you must...

options.text: Double the turns
Multiply turns by sqrt(2)
Quadruple the turns
Halve the turns

questions.explanation: Since L ∝ N^2, doubling L requires N' = sqrt2 N. Doubling N would quadruple L.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute frequency from angular speed
questions.stem: A generator coil spins at 314 rad/s; find its frequency.
questions.explanation: f = omega/(2pi) = 314/6.28 = 50 Hz. Multiplying by 2pi would be wrong.
